sentences.text: Petitions are filed seeking to quash the entire proceedings now pending in C.C.No.52292/2020 on the file of the Court of XXIX Additional CMM, Bengaluru.
4. Crl.P.No.16376/2025 is preferred by accused No.1 and Crl.P.No.11196/2023 is by accused Nos.2 and 3 respectively.
In both the petitions, parties are present before the Court and they have filed a joint memo reporting settlement.

5. In the joint memo filed in Crl.P.No.16376/2025, it is stated that as per the settlement terms, the petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.16,00,000/- to respondent No.2 as one time settlement, out of which a sum of NC: 2025:KHC:50340 HC-KAR Rs.4,00,000/- is paid today vide demand draft bearing number 718772, dated, 01.12.2025 drawn on Kotak Mahindra Bank, Thubrahalli, Branch in favour of the second respondent.

Receipt of DD has been acknowledged by the second respondent,
present before the Court.

It is further stated that as per terms of settlement, remaining amount i.e.,
Rs.12,00,000/- will be deposited before the Court of Principal Family Judge, Shivamogga, where M.C.No.390/2025 is pending.

6. Respondent No.2 / defacto complainant present before the Court, submits that in view of the settlement and in terms of the joint memo, she has no objection to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

7. In B.S. JOSHI AND OTHERS V/S. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANOTHER reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that it becomes the duty of the Court to encourage genuine settlement of matrimonial dispute and in exercise of its inherent power, High Court can quash NC: 2025:KHC:50340 HC-KAR criminal proceedings and Section 320 of the code does not limit or affect the powers under section 482 of Cr.P.C.
8.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND OTHERS V/S. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANOTHER reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in NARIDER SINGH AND OTHERS reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466 has held that when the parties have reached the settlement, and on that basis, petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to: i) secure ends of justice,
or ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

entities.text: NARIDER SINGH AND OTHERS reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Those criminal cases having overwhelming and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transaction or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family dispute should be quashed when parties have resolved their entire dispute among themselves.
9. Matter arises out of matrimonial dispute, wherein, M.C.No.390/2025 is pending before the Court of Principal Family Judge, Shivamogga.
Parties have agreed to obtain decree for divorce by way of mutual consent.

Respondent No.2 has expressed her wish not to continue with the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners and stated that she has no objection to quash NC:
2025:KHC:50340 HC-KAR the proceedings.
Hence, no useful purpose will be served in allowing the proceedings to continue against the petitioners.
In the interest of justice, it is expedient to quash the proceedings.

Accordingly, the following:-
